tickets.title: A claim on an older message that repeats an already retained message is recorded but never applied
tickets.source: accounting_agent/feed_contract.py, card_source_revision, the branch `if old and not accepted:` / `if retained:` (lines 81-85). It calls record_card_claim and returns; the sibling branch four lines below (a NEW retained message, lines 90-94) also calls apply_first_card_claim when the row had no claim. resolve_pending_supersessions only visits identities that have a SOURCE_SUPERSESSION_UNRESOLVED event, so nothing applies the claim later.
tickets.trigger: The provider's older message for a row is on file as retained evidence without a claim, and the same message (same row data, same order value) is delivered again carrying the top-level `supersedes` field. The field is outside the row data, so the message matches the retained snapshot.
minimal_reproduction: approved_locked_november(): A1 approved in November, November locked, December open
intake P = replaces A1 (2026-12-02) with its receipt -> P held under November
intake Q (2026-12-03, as_of 7) with its receipt
intake Q as_of 6, same data, no claim -> retained, changed False
intake Q as_of 6, same data, supersedes = P -> changed True; SOURCE_CLAIM_DECLARED recorded; no link, no SOURCE_SUPERSESSION_UNRESOLVED event
intake Z = replaces Q (2026-12-05) with its receipt and a tying December statement; prepare December
settlement_verified on Z; an independent reviewer approves Z; finalize December without acknowledgement
tickets.actual: Z is approved in open December and December finalizes without acknowledgement, while A1 is approved in locked November. links = [A1->P, Q->Z]; held under November = P and its receipt only. The same end state is reached when Z was approved before the claim arrived: its approval keeps governing. Without Z the state is safe but stuck: Q sits in December with SOURCE_TRANSITION_UNRESOLVED although its target is on file, it never links, and a target selection is refused ('Declared contested source target required').
tickets.expected: Clause 2: 'If the row has no claim yet, the claim applies as if it had arrived in order.' The link P->Q is made (or the claim waits as unresolved and links when P arrives), Q, Z and their receipts are held under locked November, and any earlier December approval of Q or Z stops governing at once.

observations_for_the_owner.observation: When a person selects the second target, the first target that the automatic first claim had already retired stays retired. It has no December artifact; it is listed under removed_items. Whether it should be restored is the same kind of question as U4 and is outside D-026.

An exact replay of a claim batch (same batch id, same bytes) by another person leaves no delivery record of that person (clause 5: an exact replay adds nothing), so that person is not treated as a supplier and may record the target selection. A re-send in a new envelope is recorded and is refused (C9a).

While a claimant's target has not arrived, the claimant is blocked as unresolved (clause 4), but a live row that replaces the claimant carries only the ordinary transition blocker. After settlement_verified it can be approved and December can be finalized. When the target arrives the approval stops governing at once and the replacement is held. Identical on the RD checkpoint, so not a regression and not a breach of the contract's promise; the owner may want clause 4 to cover the replacement as well.

The three disagreeing cases expect the RC review to be the latest authority. With the RD review pinned as the third authority they are obsolete, not gaps: fable_re_register_faults.py J14 to J23 show that the latest authority wins per record and that an older file cannot override it.
